A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GC-TTT research, with matching authors, core algorithm and experimental framework. All 16 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark success rates, ablations, compute-scaling experiments and runtime measurements for GC-TTT, including additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports revised benchmark results and additional original experiments, including QRL evaluations, data-selection sensitivity tests, noisy-value experiments and a policy-adaptation case study.

M1.justification: The core selection, fine-tuning and periodic-reset procedure remains intact. However, the new QRL adaptation mixes selected data with uniform samples at a 50% ratio (Appendix C.7), whereas the original objective samples exclusively from the selected dataset. Clarifications about trajectory-dependent H and pre-training estimates do not establish additional algorithm changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same medium pointmaze, antmaze and humanoidmaze expert/play tasks and cubesingle manipulation task. The new backbone, sensitivity tests and case study use this existing coverage. Larger mazes mentioned in the TTGS discussion are attributed to other work, not evaluated here.

E2.justification: v2 adds QRL as an evaluated backbone and comparator, reporting QRL with and without GC-TTT in Table 6. GC-BC, GC-IQL-DDPG, GC-IQL-AWR and SAW were already evaluated in v1. TTGS is discussed but is not added to a reported head-to-head experiment.

E3.justification: The reported main evaluation changes checkpoint averaging from 300k/350k/400k to 800k/900k/1M gradient steps. The fixed optimality quantile changes from q=0.2 to q=0.05. New protocols include fixing hyperparameters across both environments and backbones, sweeping selection parameters, and injecting Gaussian noise scaled to value estimates. These substantially expand and revise the stated evaluation design without establishing the experiments' rerun history.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity analyses for relevance threshold, return horizon and optimality quantile (Figure 7), hyperparameters shared across backbones as well as environments (Table 5), noisy-value robustness (Table 7), and a pointmaze case study showing policy changes and adaptation losses (Figure 9). These extend the retained component, training-frequency, learning-rate and model-scaling ablations.

E5.justification: v2 adds Welch's t-tests with t-statistics and p-values for all 21 main backbone/task comparisons (Appendix C.9, Table 8), beyond v1's standard errors and significance markings. It also explains the standard-error non-overlap criterion. Table 1's caption changes from three to five seeds, but Section 5 still states three; the actual main-result run count is therefore unresolved.

E6.justification: Many Table 1 means and errors change: GC-BC's baseline/+TTT averages move from 0.23/0.58 to 0.22/0.56, and GC-IQL-DDPG +TTT from 0.63 to 0.61. Revised settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting changes. New results include QRL averages of 0.47 versus 0.53 with TTT, noisy-value success rates of 0.73/0.78/0.31, and 14/21 comparisons reported significant at p<0.1. Tables 3 and 4 retain their values. Reported episode runtime also changes from approximately 85 to 70 seconds, without establishing matched timing conditions.

T1.justification: Equation 8 changes the selection predicate from value >= C to value > C, a limited mathematical-definition change affecting threshold ties. However, Algorithm 1 still uses >= C, leaving the intended rule inconsistent. The remaining core definitions, losses and FLOP derivation are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The four stated contributions and central abstract/conclusion claims remain: goal-conditioned test-time training, relevance-and-optimality data selection, improvements over pre-trained backbones, and advantages over matched-FLOP model scaling. The additional experiments support these existing claims rather than establishing a different central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the systematic-underfitting interpretation with a more qualified account involving multi-goal training dynamics and an easier local, single-goal mapping. It develops explanations of selection sensitivity and critic-noise tolerance, clarifies that periodic resets are not continual learning, and expands limitations to concentrated latency, potentially unstable policy updates, scarce data and immense state/goal spaces. Appendix E adds planning-versus-adaptation tradeoffs and their possible combination.

D1.justification: v2 adds RTX4090 hardware and operation-level timing details, explicit QRL adaptation settings, antmaze's L2 relevance distance and epsilon=1, and clarification of selection timing and trajectory-dependent H. Code access changes from a direct repository link to a project-website link. Most existing hyperparameter-table values and the FLOP calculation are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens positioning through meta-learning, model-based test-time RL and graph-based goal planning, adding discussions of Hochreiter, Finn, Nichol, Fickinger, Peng and Opryshko. New Appendix E compares GC-TTT with TTGS in computational scaling, tuning and complementarity. The DeepSeek-R1 example and reference are removed. QRL's citation already existed in v1.

P1.justification: The main six-section narrative and much of its wording remain. There are targeted explanatory rewrites, revised appendix headings, new visualization and planning-discussion sections, and relocation of implementation details from Appendix D to F. An impact statement and updated publication, correspondence and acknowledgement text are also added.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, substantially altering figure, table and algorithm placement and sizing. The original Figure 2 pipeline schematic is removed; retained figures are relocated or renumbered. New Figures 7 and 9 and Tables 5–8 add sensitivity plots, policy visualizations and experimental/statistical displays.

improvement.justification: The new selection-sensitivity and critic-noise tests better examine assumptions behind GC-TTT, while QRL validation, detailed timing and expanded limitations improve support and practical transparency. These provide a limited net gain over v1. Reporting consistency weakens, however: Table 1's five-seed caption conflicts with the three-seed text, Figure 1 retains averages that no longer match Table 1, and Equation 8 conflicts with Algorithm 1 on threshold ties. These issues temper the benefits of the added evidence.
